text: So Darius the Mede received the kingdom, at about the age of sixty-two.
It pleased Darius to appoint over the kingdom a hundred and twenty satraps, stationed throughout the realm,
and over them three administrators, one of whom was Daniel. The satraps were accountable to them, so that the king would suffer no loss.
Then this Daniel so distinguished himself above the administrators and satraps by his extraordinary spirit that the king planned to set him over the whole kingdom.

At this the administrators and satraps tried to find grounds for a charge against Daniel in his conduct of the kingdom's affairs, but they could find no charge or corruption, because he was trustworthy; no negligence or corruption was found in him.
So these men said, "We will never find any charge against this Daniel unless we find it in connection with the law of his God."
Then these administrators and satraps came as a body to the king and said to him: "King Darius, live forever!

All the royal administrators, prefects, satraps, counselors, and governors have agreed that the king should issue a decree and enforce a ban: that anyone who prays to any god or human being during the next thirty days, except to you, O king, shall be thrown into the lions' den.
Now, O king, issue the ban and sign the document, so that it cannot be altered—in accordance with the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed."
So King Darius signed the document containing the ban.

Now when Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went home to his upper room, where the windows opened toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he got down on his knees and prayed, giving thanks to his God, just as he had always done.

versions.text: Now when Daniel learned that the document had been signed, he went into his house, where the upstairs windows opened toward Jerusalem, and three times a day he got down on his knees and prayed, giving thanks to his God, just as he had always done.
versions.explanation: The Aramaic specifies an upper chamber (עִלִּיתֵהּ) in which the windows stood open; 'upstairs windows' blurs the detail of the roof-chamber where Daniel prayed. The revision keeps the oral rhythm while preserving the image.

text: Then these men came as a body and found Daniel praying and pleading before his God.

So they went to the king and spoke to him about his royal ban: "Did you not sign a ban that during the next thirty days anyone who prays to any god or human being except to you, O king, would be thrown into the lions' den?" The king answered, "The matter stands firm, in accordance with the law of the Medes and Persians, which cannot be repealed."
Then they said to the king, "Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah, pays no attention to you, O king, or to the ban you have signed. Three times a day he makes his petition."

versions.text: Then they said to the king, "Daniel, one of the exiles from Judah, pays no attention to you, O king, or to the ban you have signed. Three times a day he says his prayers."
versions.explanation: 'Says his prayers' sounds colloquial and slightly dismissive; the Aramaic idiom (בָּעֵא בָּעוּתֵהּ) means to make petition, matching the accusers' legal framing of the charge.

text: When the king heard this, he was deeply distressed; he set his mind on rescuing Daniel and labored until sundown to save him.
Then these men came as a body to the king and said to him, "Know, O king, that by the law of the Medes and Persians no ban or decree the king issues can be changed."

versions.text: Then these men came as a body to the king and said to him, "Remember, O king, that by the law of the Medes and Persians no ban or decree the king issues can be changed."
versions.explanation: The verb דַּע means 'know' (be aware), not 'remember'. The accusers are pressing a legal fact on the king rather than recalling something to his memory.

text: So the king gave the order, and they brought Daniel and threw him into the lions' den. The king said to Daniel, "May your God, whom you serve continually, rescue you!"
A stone was brought and placed over the mouth of the den, and the king sealed it with his own signet ring and with the rings of his nobles, so that nothing concerning Daniel could be changed.
Then the king returned to his palace and spent the night fasting; no entertainment was brought before him, and sleep fled from him.
At the first light of dawn the king got up and hurried to the lions' den.
When he came near the den, he called out to Daniel in an anguished voice, "Daniel, servant of the living God, has your God, whom you serve continually, been able to rescue you from the lions?"
Daniel answered, "O king, live forever!
My God sent his angel and shut the mouths of the lions, and they have not harmed me, because I was found innocent before him. And before you too, O king, I have done no wrong."
The king was overjoyed and gave orders to lift Daniel out of the den. So Daniel was lifted out, and no wound was found on him, because he had trusted in his God.

Then at the king's command the men who had accused Daniel were brought in and thrown into the lions' den, along with their children and their wives. And before they reached the floor of the den, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.

versions.text: Then at the king's command the men who had accused Daniel were brought in and thrown into the lions' den, along with their wives and children. And before they reached the floor of the den, the lions overpowered them and crushed all their bones.
versions.explanation: The Aramaic lists 'their children and their wives' in that order; keeping the original sequence is a small gain in accuracy and costs nothing in flow.

text: Then King Darius wrote to all the peoples, nations, and languages who dwell in all the earth: "May your peace abound!

I hereby decree that in every part of my kingdom people are to tremble and stand in awe before the God of Daniel. For he is the living God, enduring forever; his kingdom will never be destroyed, and his dominion has no end.
He rescues and he saves; he works signs and wonders in the heavens and on the earth. He has rescued Daniel from the power of the lions."
So this Daniel prospered during the reign of Darius and the reign of Cyrus the Persian.
